methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Amca, a robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jai Malik and Eli Giovanetti, is preparing for IPO following $76.5M in total capital raised. The valuation landscape consists of a narrow peer universe: one public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private-stage robotics companies, including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

Traditional peer-median valuation proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the robotics and manufacturing sector. The analysis identified 11 same-sector peers overall, but none met the minimum threshold of three datapoints when filtered for stage alignment or valuation tier similarity. A broad sector median would introduce excessive noise given the heterogeneity of robotics business models and development stages.

The sparse comp environment and absence of a robust triangulation methodology leaves the valuation range indeterminate from the data available. Key uncertainties center on the representativeness of the single public comparable and the stage and valuation dynamics of the eight private peers relative to Amca's specific market position and financial profile. IPO pricing will likely depend on underwriter roadshow feedback, recent comparable transaction multiples, and forward revenue/growth assumptions not captured in this peer framework. Additional disclosure of Amca's revenue, growth rate, and profitability profile would be necessary to construct a defensible valuation range.
